faqs.question: Are advanced prompting techniques still needed with reasoning models?
faqs.answer: Some less than before. Explicit chain-of-thought adds little on reasoning models. Techniques that bring in information or checks the model cannot produce alone (tools, retrieval, code execution, schema validation, independent verification and evaluation sets) remain valuable.

faqs.question: What is the difference between prompt engineering and context engineering?
faqs.answer: Prompt engineering focuses on writing the instructions. Context engineering covers everything that enters the model's context window at each step: instructions, tool definitions, retrieved documents, conversation history, memory and examples (Anthropic, 2025).

faqs.question: Should I fine-tune instead of using advanced prompts?
faqs.answer: Try prompting, retrieval and evaluation first: they are faster to change and do not require training data. Fine-tuning becomes worth considering when you have a stable task, many high-quality examples and a measured gap that prompting cannot close.

faqs.question: Which AI model is best for coding?
faqs.answer: It changes every few months and depends on the task, language and tool. Rather than relying on leaderboards, try two or three assistants on a handful of real tasks from your own codebase and compare the diffs you would actually merge.

faqs.question: Should I use a chat assistant or a coding agent?
faqs.answer: Chat is good for explanations, small functions and reviewing snippets. Agents that can read the repository, run commands and tests are better for multi-file changes, but need clearer instructions, a rules file and careful review of their diffs.

faqs.question: Do I still need to learn to code if AI writes code?
faqs.answer: Yes. You need to specify the problem, judge whether the output is correct and secure, and debug it when it is not. All of the prompts above assume you can read the code that comes back. Our Python projects for beginners is a good place to build that foundation.

faqs.question: What is the best prompt format for ChatGPT?
faqs.answer: There is no single best format. A reliable pattern is: the goal in one sentence, the context and your material, the format you want, and any limits. For longer prompts, separate sections with headings or labels so ChatGPT can tell your instructions apart from pasted text.

faqs.question: How long should a ChatGPT prompt be?
faqs.answer: As long as it needs to be to remove guessing, and no longer. A one-line request is fine for simple tasks. A prompt for a report or a plan may be several paragraphs, mostly made up of context and source material.

faqs.question: Why does ChatGPT give different answers to the same prompt?
faqs.answer: The model generates text with some randomness, and memory, custom instructions and earlier messages in the chat also affect the answer. If you need consistency, give a precise format and an example, and start from a clean chat.

faqs.question: Is it safe to put personal information into ChatGPT?
faqs.answer: Treat it like any online service. Avoid sharing passwords, government ID numbers, financial account details and other people's private information, review your memory and data control settings, and follow your workplace rules for work data.

faqs.answer: Drafting, rewriting, summarizing, extracting structure from messy notes, brainstorming and preparing for conversations. These are tasks where you can quickly judge the result. Be more careful with tasks that depend on facts, calculations or judgment the assistant cannot verify.

faqs.question: How do I get AI to write in my company's voice?
faqs.answer: Paste two or three real examples of your best writing and ask it to match their tone, length and structure. Examples work better than adjectives like "professional but friendly". In ChatGPT, you can save the examples in project instructions or files so every chat uses them; see our ChatGPT tips for beginners.

faqs.question: Can I paste confidential business data into AI tools?

faqs.question: What is prompt engineering?
faqs.answer: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing the instructions, context and examples you give an AI model so that it produces useful, reliable output. It ranges from writing a clearer chat message to designing and testing the system prompts that run inside software products.

faqs.question: Which prompt engineering technique matters most?
faqs.answer: Being clear and specific about the goal, audience, context and format. A systematic survey of prompting research found few-shot examples and chain-of-thought to be the most widely used techniques (Schulhoff et al., 2024), but both build on a clear instruction.

faqs.question: Do these techniques work the same on every model?
faqs.answer: Mostly, but not exactly. Clear instructions, context, examples and structure help across models. Reasoning-related techniques differ: step-by-step prompts help non-reasoning models more than reasoning models, and some features, such as prefilling the answer, are model-specific. Check the vendor's prompting guide and test.

faqs.question: Is prompt engineering still useful as models improve?
faqs.answer: Yes, though its focus is shifting. Models need fewer tricks, but they still cannot read your mind about goals, audience or facts they were never given. Anthropic describes the next step as context engineering: choosing everything that goes into the model's context, not just the wording of the instructions (Anthropic, 2025).

faqs.question: What are the basic principles of economics?
faqs.answer: The core ideas are scarcity, opportunity cost, marginal thinking and incentives (how individuals decide); trade, prices and market failure (how people interact); and productivity, money and short-run trade-offs (how the whole economy works). Mankiw's "ten principles of economics" is the best-known short list.

faqs.question: What is the most important economic principle?
faqs.answer: Opportunity cost is the most useful in daily life, because it applies to every choice: the real cost of anything is the best alternative you give up. For the economy as a whole, productivity matters most over the long run.

faqs.question: Are economic principles always true?
faqs.answer: No. They are good first approximations that describe how people tend to behave on average. Behavioral economics shows that people often depart from them, and every principle above has known limits. Use them as a starting point for thinking, not as laws of nature.

faqs.question: What are the basic concepts of economics?
faqs.answer: The foundations are scarcity, opportunity cost, incentives, supply and demand, and trade, which we cover in 15 basic economic principles. Beyond those, beginners should know elasticity, market structure, inflation, interest rates, GDP, unemployment, and monetary and fiscal policy.

faqs.question: What is the difference between monetary and fiscal policy?
faqs.answer: Monetary policy is run by a central bank, which sets interest rates and controls the money supply. Fiscal policy is run by the government, through taxes and spending. Both aim to keep the economy stable, but they use different tools and are decided by different institutions.

faqs.question: What economic concepts matter most in 2026?
faqs.answer: The big themes of 2026 are the energy supply shock and its effect on inflation, central banks raising rates again, high government debt, tariffs and trade, and the economic impact of AI investment. Concepts 15 and 25 to 29 above explain each of these.

faqs.question: How can a beginner learn economics?
faqs.answer: Start with a short list of concepts like this one, then follow real data releases and news with those concepts in mind. Free courses from universities and central bank education pages are good next steps, and a standard introductory textbook covers everything here in more depth.

faqs.question: What are the most important economic indicators?
faqs.answer: For a quick read on any economy, watch real GDP growth, the unemployment rate, inflation (CPI or PCE), and the central bank's policy rate. Add PMIs and jobless claims for early warning signs.

faqs.question: Which indicators predict a recession?
faqs.answer: No indicator predicts recessions reliably on its own. The most watched warning signs are an inverted yield curve, rising jobless claims, PMI new orders below 50, falling building permits, and the Sahm rule based on unemployment. A recession is more likely when several of these point the same way.

faqs.question: Where can I find economic data for free?
faqs.answer: National statistics offices and central banks publish their data free of charge. For the U.S., the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis's FRED database collects hundreds of thousands of series in one place. For global comparisons, use the IMF World Economic Outlook database, the World Bank's data site and the OECD.

faqs.question: What is inflation in simple words?
faqs.answer: Inflation is when prices across the economy rise over time, so the same amount of money buys less. If inflation is 3.7%, something that cost \$100 a year ago costs about \$103.70 today on average.

faqs.question: Who is hurt most by inflation?
faqs.answer: People whose income or savings do not keep up: those on fixed pensions, savers with money in low-interest accounts, workers without bargaining power, and households that spend a large share of income on food and energy. People with variable-rate debt are also hurt when interest rates rise.

faqs.question: Does inflation ever help anyone?
faqs.answer: Yes. Borrowers with fixed-rate debt repay with money worth less than when they borrowed. Owners of assets whose value rises with prices, such as some property and businesses, can also come out ahead. Governments with large debts benefit in a similar way.

faqs.question: Will prices go back down when inflation falls?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Lower inflation means prices rise more slowly, not that they fall. Individual items can get cheaper, as eggs did in 2026, but a broad fall in prices (deflation) is rare and often a sign of a weak economy. The realistic goal is for incomes to catch up with prices.

faqs.question: What is a simple example of supply and demand?
faqs.answer: Concert tickets. When a famous band plays a small venue, many more people want tickets than there are seats, so tickets sell out and resale prices climb. If the same band played a huge stadium on a weeknight, there would be more seats than buyers and prices would have to drop.

faqs.question: What is the law of supply and demand?
faqs.answer: The law of demand says that, other things equal, people buy less of something when its price rises. The law of supply says sellers offer more when the price rises. Together, they predict that the price will move toward the level where the amount demanded equals the amount supplied.

faqs.question: Why do prices go up quickly but come down slowly?
faqs.answer: Sellers often buy inputs under long-term contracts, face costs like wages that rarely fall, and may test how much customers will accept. Retail chocolate prices staying high after cocoa prices fell is a recent example. Competition usually brings prices down eventually, but the lag can last months.

title: PHP2Shell Explained: Critical PHP Security Vulnerabilities, CVEs, and How to Fix Them (2026)
seoTitle: PHP2Shell Explained: CVEs, Affected Versions and Fixes
description: What PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) is, which PHP versions and setups are affected, and how to patch, mitigate and check for compromise.
author: BlogAI Editors

faqs.question: Does PHP2Shell affect WordPress sites?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the server's PHP is unpatched. The flaw is in PHP, not WordPress, so updating WordPress or its plugins does not fix it. Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated code execution against WordPress, Drupal and Joomla (Wiz). On managed or shared hosting, your host has to update PHP; check with them.

faqs.question: Is disabling session.upload_progress enough?
faqs.answer: No. It blocks one known path for CVE-2026-109619, but it does nothing for CVE-2026-109618, and PHP says no configuration change fully mitigates either flaw (GHSA-6wmf). Use it as a stopgap and keep it off after patching if you do not need upload progress.

faqs.question: My server shows an older PHP version. Am I vulnerable?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Distribution packages often backport the fix without changing the upstream version number. Check the package changelog or your distribution's security tracker for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.

faqs.question: Do I need to restart after updating?
faqs.answer: Yes. Running PHP-FPM pools and Apache processes keep the old code in memory until they restart.

faqs.question: Is PHP 7.4 or 8.1 still safe to run?
faqs.answer: They are end of life, so PHP.net does not ship fixed releases for them. Minimal source patches and some vendor backports exist, but the long-term fix is upgrading to a supported branch (8.2 or newer).

faqs.question: How can I make money from home with no money?
faqs.answer: Use what you already have: sell items you no longer need, freelance a skill, tutor, or take paid studies and usability tests. All of these can start with a phone or computer and no upfront spending.

faqs.question: What home-based work is legitimate?
faqs.answer: Work where a real customer pays for a real product or service: freelancing, tutoring, selling goods, caring for pets or children with any required license, and employee jobs listed on a company's own website. Be wary of anything that requires payment to start or promises high pay for little work.

faqs.question: Do I need a license to sell food or run a business from home?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, depending on what you do and where you live. Food sales, childcare, hair and beauty services, and businesses with customer visits are commonly regulated. Check with your city or county and your state's licensing agencies.

faqs.question: How much can I earn from home?
faqs.answer: It varies too much to give a reliable figure. Freelancing and tutoring are paid per project or hour and can grow with skill; reselling and crafts depend on margins and volume; studies and testing pay small amounts.

faqs.question: How much can a beginner make online?
faqs.answer: There is no honest single number. Freelancers who already have a marketable skill can earn their first few hundred dollars within weeks; studies and testing usually bring in small amounts; audience businesses often earn little in the first six months and then vary from nothing to a full income. Anyone who promises a specific figure is selling something.

faqs.question: What is the fastest way to make money online?
faqs.answer: For most people, freelancing a skill you already have, online tutoring, or selling items you already own. Each pays as soon as the work or sale is done, rather than after an audience builds up.

faqs.question: Can I make money online without spending anything?
faqs.answer: Yes. Freelancing, tutoring, research studies, testing and selling your own items can all start at \$0 with a computer and an internet connection. If a "free opportunity" asks for payment to unlock earnings, it is not free and is very likely a scam.

faqs.question: Do I have to pay taxes on small online earnings?
faqs.answer: In the U.S., yes: all income is reportable, even without a 1099 form, and self-employment tax applies once net self-employment earnings reach \$400 in a year (IRS). Rules differ in other countries.

faqs.question: How much should I have saved by 30?
faqs.answer: Fidelity's guideline is about one times your annual salary saved for retirement by age 30, assuming you start saving 15% of income at 25 (Fidelity). Many people are behind that at 30; raising your savings rate is the fix.

faqs.question: Should I invest or pay off student loans first in my 20s?
faqs.answer: Get any employer match first, since it is an immediate return. Then compare rates: high-interest private loans and credit cards usually come before extra investing; low-rate federal loans can often be paid on schedule while you invest. Check your federal repayment options at StudentAid.gov.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start managing money at 29?
faqs.answer: No. Starting at 29 still gives decades of compounding. The best time to start is when you read this; the second best is next payday.

faqs.question: What is the first step in managing money?
faqs.answer: Find out where your money goes. Track a full month of spending and compare it with your take-home pay. Every other decision, from budgeting to investing, depends on knowing your real cash flow.

faqs.question: Should I save or pay off debt first?
faqs.answer: Usually both, in order: build a small emergency fund first so you do not need to borrow again, collect any employer match, then put extra money toward high-interest debt such as credit cards. Low-interest debt, such as many mortgages, can be paid on schedule while you invest.

faqs.question: How much of my income should I save?
faqs.answer: There is no single right number. Common guidelines include 20% of take-home pay in the 50/30/20 framework, or Fidelity's current guideline of 15% of pre-tax income for retirement (including any employer match) plus 10% of take-home pay for near-term goals and emergency savings (Fidelity). Start with what you can and raise it over time.

faqs.question: What is the easiest passive income for beginners?
faqs.answer: Interest on savings and regular investing in a broad index fund. Both can be set up in an afternoon and automated. They grow slowly at first, which is why starting early matters.

faqs.question: How much money do I need to make \$1,000 a month in passive income?
faqs.answer: At a 4% yield or withdrawal rate, about \$300,000 (\$12,000 a year ÷ 0.04). At lower yields it takes more. Building that much usually takes years of consistent saving and investing.

faqs.question: Is passive income taxed?
faqs.answer: Yes, in most countries. In the U.S., interest and most rental and royalty income are taxed as ordinary income, qualified dividends and long-term capital gains get lower rates, and retirement accounts change when tax is due. Treasury interest is exempt from state and local tax.

faqs.question: Is real estate really passive income?
faqs.answer: Rarely at first. Owning rental property involves finding tenants, repairs and finances. A property manager makes it closer to passive at the cost of part of the rent; REITs are the most passive way to own real estate.

faqs.question: Are personal finance rules of thumb reliable?
faqs.answer: They are reliable as starting points, not as personal plans. Each one has assumptions about your age, income, interest rates and goals. Use them to spot problems, such as housing at 45% of income or no emergency savings, and adjust the numbers to your situation.

faqs.question: What is the most important personal finance rule?
faqs.answer: Spend less than you earn. Without a monthly surplus, you cannot build savings, pay down debt or invest, and every other rule depends on it.

faqs.question: Is the 4% rule still valid in 2026?
faqs.answer: It remains a widely used starting point, but its author called it a conservative floor based on historical U.S. data, and it assumes a 30-year retirement without fees or taxes. Early retirees and people with very different portfolios should plan with more care, ideally with a fee-only planner.

faqs.question: What is the best side hustle for someone with a full-time job?
faqs.answer: The one that uses a skill you already have and runs on your own schedule. For professionals that is usually freelancing; for others, tutoring, babysitting, pet sitting or flexible delivery work are easy to start.

faqs.question: How many hours should a side hustle take?
faqs.answer: There is no rule, but five to ten hours a week is a common, sustainable range. Track your energy and your day-job performance as well as your earnings.

faqs.question: Do I need to tell my employer about my side hustle?
faqs.answer: It depends on your contract and local law. Read your employment agreement and handbook for outside-work, conflict-of-interest and intellectual-property clauses. When a clause applies or you are unsure, ask before starting.

faqs.question: How do I pay taxes on side hustle income?
faqs.answer: In the U.S., report it on your return (usually Schedule C), and either make quarterly estimated payments or increase withholding at your day job with a new Form W-4 (IRS). Keep records of income and deductible expenses such as business mileage.

faqs.question: What are the most important money habits?
faqs.answer: Spending less than you earn, saving automatically on payday, paying credit cards in full, investing regularly in low-cost diversified funds, and reviewing your finances on a schedule. Most other habits support one of these.

faqs.question: How long does it take to build a money habit?
faqs.answer: In one well-known study, new daily habits took an average of 66 days to feel automatic, with wide variation between people. Automating a habit, such as a savings transfer, makes it work from day one.

faqs.question: What does financial freedom mean?
faqs.answer: It usually means having enough savings and investments that you could cover your living costs without needing a paycheck, so working becomes a choice. It is reached gradually by saving a meaningful share of income for many years and investing it well.

faqs.question: Will AI take my job?
faqs.answer: For most people, the evidence through 2026 shows AI changing tasks within jobs rather than eliminating them. The risk is highest for entry-level roles in exposed occupations such as customer support and junior software development, and for freelance writing and similar work bought task by task.

faqs.question: Which jobs are most exposed to AI?
faqs.answer: Clerical, customer service, writing, translation, programming and some financial and legal analysis tasks are most exposed according to the ILO and IMF indexes. Exposure means AI can perform some tasks, which can raise or lower demand for the job.

faqs.question: Which skills matter most?
faqs.answer: The studies here point to judgment about when AI is wrong, deep domain expertise, the ability to specify and review work, and the human skills of explaining, persuading and caring for people.
